# S6 — Re-generate auto-generated submission files

## Which files are auto-generated

These four files in `D:\SimSat\` are outputs of scripts, not hand-maintained docs:

| File | Generated by | Trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `SUBMISSION_PACKET.md` | `scripts/submission_evidence.py` | Needs latest encounter-eval + pinned casebook labels |
| `SUBMISSION_READINESS.md` | `scripts/submission_readiness.py` | Needs the packet + casebook + image assets to exist |
| `SUBMISSION_CASEBOOK.md` | `scripts/submission_casebook.py` | Needs pinned operator-review labels on the 3 submission cases |
| `REVIEW_QUEUE.md` | `scripts/review_queue_casebook.py` | Needs running Django + trace store |
| `REVIEW_SET_BUILD.md` | (likely) `scripts/review_set_build.py` or similar internal tooling | Needs the sweep planner |

Phase 4 does **not** ship hand-edited replacements for any of these. If we did, the next run of the generator would clobber our edits.

## What to regenerate and when

### After applying Phase 1 fixes

Phase 1 fixes the tzinfo bug at `src/sim/simulator.py:111`. That bug phase-shifts encounter windows in non-UTC environments, which means the `SUBMISSION_PACKET.md` scorecard was built against slightly-wrong timestamps if the stack ran in a non-UTC shell. After Phase 1 lands, regenerate:

```bash
# Recompute encounter eval for the scorecard
python scripts/encounter_eval.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/sim --scenario-sweep --top-k 8 --materialize-top-k 2

# Re-materialize the packet (prefers reviewed labels, falls back to simulated_submission_case)
python scripts/submission_evidence.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/sim
```

### After applying Phase 4 / S3 casebook re-labels

S3 re-labels the 3 pinned cases via `operator_review.py` with observable-evidence notes. After running those, regenerate:

```bash
# New casebook reflects the new notes
python scripts/submission_casebook.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/sim

# Strict reviewed-only packet (fails if any pack still lacks a pinned reviewed case)
python scripts/submission_evidence.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/sim --reviewed-only

# Readiness check across packet + casebook + image assets + runtime honesty
python scripts/submission_readiness.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/sim
```

### After Phase 2 / S3 rematerialize-clip-local

Phase 2 `S3-rematerialize-clip-local` re-runs the 3 pinned cases under the current `clip_local` backend so the casebook's `Observation runtime: stub` becomes `Observation runtime: clip_local`. After running that phase, regenerate the casebook:

```bash
python scripts/submission_casebook.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/sim
```

Visually diff the new casebook against the version in `phase-4/S3-casebook-notes/SUBMISSION_CASEBOOK.md` (that reference was written assuming `Observation runtime: stub` from historical traces). The new generated version should show `clip_local` once Phase 2 S3 has been applied.

## Review queue

`REVIEW_QUEUE.md` (40 KB) changes with every fresh review sweep. Don't worry about fighting for a clean diff — regenerate it after Phase 1 to pick up the tzinfo fix, then again after any new pinned cases are added:

```bash
python scripts/review_queue_casebook.py --inprocess
```

## Review set build

`REVIEW_SET_BUILD.md` documents the most recent sweep attempt. Today's sweep logged `quality_skips=60, added_distinct=0` for all 3 targets — either a dedup bug or genuinely deterministic SSO windows. This is Tier-3 "Nice to Have" from the review punch list (see Known Issues). Debugging the sweep is the trigger for a fresh REVIEW_SET_BUILD.md; don't regenerate before investigating or the next run will re-log the same empty result.

## Final readiness gate

Once all of Phase 1-4 are applied, a green readiness check looks like:

```bash
python scripts/submission_readiness.py --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/sim
# expected output:
#   Sentinel enabled: True
#   Mapbox enabled: False
#   ObservationVLA runtime: clip_local
#   Pinned submission cases: 3
#   Scenario Status: all rows reviewed_ready=True
```

If any row shows `reviewed_ready=False`, the matching case still needs an `operator_review.py` re-label plus casebook regeneration.
